issues.t: Automatic transmission slips or loses gears
issues.sym: The truck flares in RPM between shifts, shifts late or hard, slips, or loses one or more gears. The check engine light may come on.
issues.why: The 4L60-E four-speed automatic in these trucks is known for internal wear. NHTSA looked into damaged 2-4 bands and 3-4 clutches in this transmission, and GM issued bulletins for slipping and wrong shifts.
issues.next: Check the fluid level and smell. If it slips or a gear is missing, stop towing and have a transmission shop diagnose it before more parts are damaged.

issues.t: Intake manifold gasket leaks coolant
issues.sym: Coolant level keeps dropping, a sweet smell, white smoke on a cold start, milky oil, rough idle or the temperature gauge climbing.
issues.why: The plastic-type intake manifold gaskets break down with heat and age, and the factory DEX-COOL coolant is widely blamed for speeding this up. Coolant can leak outside or into the oil.
issues.next: Watch the coolant level. If it keeps dropping or the oil looks milky, stop driving and have the gaskets replaced before coolant damages the engine bearings.

issues.t: Four-wheel drive won't engage or works on and off
issues.sym: Pressing the 4WD button does nothing, the 4WD light flashes, the truck won't move in 4WD, or it slips and makes noise in 4WD.
issues.why: The push-button 4WD system relies on a front axle actuator, a transfer case shift motor and an electronic control module. Owners report replacing actuators and control modules, and GM issued bulletins for 4WD that won't engage or slips.
issues.next: Have a shop scan the 4WD system and test the front axle actuator and transfer case motor before replacing parts. Don't rely on 4WD in snow until it is fixed.

issues.t: ABS warning light on from brake control module failure
issues.sym: The ABS light stays on and the anti-lock brakes stop working. Normal braking usually still works.
issues.why: The most reported Sonoma problem on RepairPal is an internal failure in the electronic brake control module, the computer that runs the ABS.
issues.next: Have the ABS codes read. If the module is at fault, a rebuilt module is an option besides a new one. Drive carefully on slippery roads in the meantime.

issues.t: Rusted brake lines
issues.sym: A soft or sinking brake pedal, brake fluid wet spots along the frame or near the rear axle, or a brake warning light that comes and goes.
issues.why: The steel brake lines rust where they touch frame clips, especially the section over the rear axle, on trucks driven where roads are salted. A rusted line can burst under hard braking.
issues.next: Have the brake lines inspected, especially in snow-belt states. Replace any rusted line right away, and don't drive with a soft pedal.

issues.t: Fuel pump fails or fuel gauge reads wrong
issues.sym: No-start (often when hot), stalling at idle with low fuel, a whine from under the bed, or a fuel gauge that reads empty or jumps around.
issues.why: The in-tank fuel pump wears out and the fuel level sender in the same assembly corrodes. Both are replaced by dropping the tank.
issues.next: If the truck cranks but won't start, have fuel pressure tested. Replacing the pump and sender together avoids paying for the tank work twice.

issues.t: Engine loses power from clogged fuel pump strainer
issues.sym: The engine stumbles, loses power or stalls, often under load or with a low tank.
issues.why: NHTSA looked into fuel starvation caused by a clogged strainer on the in-tank fuel pump. GM changed the strainer design.
issues.next: If the engine loses power under load, have the fuel pressure checked. The pump and its strainer are replaced together.

issues.t: Steering gearbox leaks and gets loose
issues.sym: Power steering fluid drips from the frame rail near the left front wheel, the truck wanders on the highway, or the steering wheel has extra play.
issues.why: The seals in the steering gearbox leak and its internal parts wear. GM offers a seal service kit for the pitman arm shaft.
issues.next: Keep the power steering fluid topped up and have the gearbox checked. A seal kit can fix leaks; a worn box needs replacing.

issues.t: Misfire from worn distributor cap and rotor
issues.sym: Misfires and stumbling, especially in damp weather, a flashing or steady check engine light, rough running or stalling.
issues.why: Moisture causes carbon tracks inside the distributor cap on the 4.3L V6, and internal distributor faults are among the more common reported problems.
issues.next: Have the cap, rotor and plug wires inspected. Replacing them is a simple first step for misfires on this engine.

issues.t: Lower engine knock on the 4.3L V6
issues.sym: A knocking or rattling from the bottom of the engine that gets louder with load or as the engine wears.
issues.why: Worn piston skirts or bearings in the 4.3L V6 can make a knock. GM also issued a bulletin for engine rattle on these trucks.
issues.next: Check the oil level and pressure. If the knock is deep or getting worse, have a shop diagnose it before it leads to engine failure.

issues.t: Random misfire code with no misfire felt
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on with a random-misfire code, but the engine seems to run fine.
issues.why: GM issued a bulletin for the 4.3L V6 setting a P0300 random-misfire code without a real misfire.
issues.next: Have the codes read and ask the shop to check GM's bulletin before replacing ignition parts.

issues.t: Clicks but won't crank in cold weather
issues.sym: On cold mornings, below about 20°F, the engine clicks or won't crank or start. It may start fine when warmer.
issues.why: GM issued bulletins for 2001 trucks that won't crank or start in the cold, including a click/no-start on the 4.3L V6.
issues.next: Make sure the battery and cables are in good shape, then have a dealer or shop check the GM bulletin for your truck.

issues.t: Third door handle breaks on extended cab
issues.sym: The handle on the rear third door of the extended cab takes a lot of force, breaks, or the door won't latch or open.
issues.why: GM issued bulletins for third door handles that need too much effort or break on extended cab pickups.
issues.next: Have the handle and latch replaced. Don't force a stuck door; the latch rods can bend.

issues.t: Outside door handle breaks
issues.sym: The outside door handle snaps or stops opening the door.
issues.why: The plastic exterior door handles crack with age and use, which owners report at fairly low mileage.
issues.next: Replace the handle; you can usually open the door from inside in the meantime.

issues.t: Alternator fails
issues.sym: Battery light, dimming lights, a dead battery or the truck dying while driving.
issues.why: Owners report alternator failures around 88,000 miles on average.
issues.next: Have the charging system tested before replacing the battery. A failing alternator will drain a new battery too.

issues.t: Front brake caliper sticks
issues.sym: The truck pulls to one side, a wheel gets very hot, a burning smell after driving or uneven pad wear.
issues.why: Owners report front brake calipers locking up. A stuck caliper keeps the pad pressed on the rotor.
issues.next: Have the brakes checked soon. Replace the stuck caliper and the pads and rotor on that axle if they overheated.

issues.t: Heater or fan stops working on some speeds
issues.sym: The blower fan works only on high or not at all, or the heater or A/C stops blowing the right temperature.
issues.why: The blower motor resistor, which sets the lower fan speeds, burns out. GM also issued bulletins for heaters blowing warm or cold air incorrectly.
issues.next: If only high speed works, replace the blower resistor. For no heat or no A/C, have the system diagnosed.

issues.t: Fuel pump nozzle clicks off and tank is slow to fill
issues.sym: Fuel backs up the filler neck and the pump nozzle keeps clicking off, so filling up takes a long time.
issues.why: The tank cannot vent air fast enough, usually because a part in the evaporative emissions (EVAP) vent system is blocked or has failed.
issues.next: Have the EVAP vent valve, charcoal canister and hoses checked. Don't top off past the first click.

issues.t: Flex-fuel sensor fails on the 2.2L
issues.sym: Check engine light, poor running or hard starting on a flex-fuel (E85-capable) truck.
issues.why: Flex-fuel 2.2L trucks use a sensor in the fuel line to measure ethanol content. Owners report this sensor failing at high mileage.
issues.next: Have the codes read. If the flex-fuel sensor is at fault, replacing it usually fixes the running problem.

issues.t: Fuel tank rusts through and leaks
issues.sym: A strong gas smell and fuel dripping from under the truck, often near the tank.
issues.why: Owners report the steel fuel tank rusting through around 65,000 miles.
issues.next: Park outside, don't smoke near it and get it towed to a shop. A leaking tank is a fire risk and must be replaced.

issues.t: Brake line can rub on the oil pan (recall)
issues.sym: Brake fluid leak near the left side of the engine, a soft pedal and longer stops.
issues.why: On some 4.3L trucks, the front brake line could rub the oil pan and wear through.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. A dealer adds a clip or replaces the line for free.

issues.t: Seat belt webbing may separate (recall)
issues.sym: No warning signs. In a frontal crash the belt webbing could separate.
issues.why: On extended cabs with 60/40 bench seats and some trucks with reclining bucket seats, the seat recliner could cut the belt webbing.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. The dealer installs a protective cover for free.

issues.t: Brake pipe nuts may loosen and leak (recall)
issues.sym: Brake fluid leak near the ABS unit, a soft pedal or a brake warning light.
issues.why: On some 2WD trucks, brake pipe nuts at the ABS unit were not tightened enough and could work loose.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. The dealer inspects the fittings and repairs them for free.

issues.t: ABS motor clip can disable ABS (recall)
issues.sym: The ABS warning light comes on and the anti-lock function stops working.
issues.why: On some trucks with four-wheel disc brakes, a spring clip in the ABS motor was out of spec and could let the motor bearing shift.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. The dealer replaces the ABS valve assembly for free.

issues.t: Door label shows wrong payload (recall)
issues.sym: No driving symptom. The door label lists more payload than the truck is rated to carry.
issues.why: Some labels overstated maximum payload. A truck loaded to that weight may not handle as expected.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and get the corrected label. Don't overload the truck.

issues.t: Seat belt buckles may not hold in a crash (recall)
issues.sym: No warning signs. The buckle could fail under crash loads.
issues.why: Some buckle bases were not heat-treated properly and may not meet federal strength rules.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. The dealer checks the buckle date codes and replaces them for free.

issues.t: Airbag warning label has wrong information (recall)
issues.sym: No driving symptom. The airbag caution label has incorrect information.
issues.why: Some trucks were built with labels that do not meet federal airbag labeling rules.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls; GMC sends the correct labels for free.
